summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea, asthma, and obesity, was admitted for a 2.5-week worsening of left lower back and sacroiliac pain consistent with an inflammatory flare. He had received 60 mg of prednisone at an outside hospital with partial relief and reported associated eye irritation concerning for possible iritis. On admission, he was treated with continued OxyContin, oxycodone for breakthrough pain, lidocaine patch, and a short course of prednisone with GI protection using sucralfate and omeprazole. Ophthalmology evaluated his eye symptoms and found no evidence of iritis, attributing the discomfort to dry eyes. His pain improved during the hospitalization, and he was discharged home on a tapering dose of prednisone, sucralfate, acetaminophen, and his baseline medications, with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider and rheumatology for long-term management.
